claims.text: Palladium nanoparticle surface area governs catalytic activity.
Palladium nanoparticle surface area governs catalytic selectivity.
Palladium nanoparticle lattice strain governs catalytic activity.
Palladium nanoparticle lattice strain governs catalytic selectivity.
Surface area and lattice strain influence adsorption and desorption of reactants and products.
Changes in adsorption and desorption caused by surface area and lattice strain lead to changes in catalytic activity and selectivity.
Catalytic activity is positively correlated with palladium nanoparticle surface area and lattice strain.
Catalytic selectivity is positively correlated with palladium nanoparticle surface area and lattice strain.
Smaller palladium nanoparticles have higher surface areas and lattice strain than the larger-particle baseline.
Smaller palladium nanoparticles exhibit higher catalytic activity than the larger-particle baseline because they provide more active sites.
Smaller palladium nanoparticles exhibit higher catalytic selectivity than the larger-particle baseline because they provide more active sites.
Impurities or defects may influence catalytic activity and selectivity.
The proposed comparison systematically varies palladium nanoparticle size and shape while holding temperature, pressure, and reactant concentration constant.
Failure to observe a correlation of surface area and lattice strain with catalytic activity and selectivity would falsify the hypothesis.
